findings.title: Table1 diagnosis counts exceed n
findings.description: The seven ICD-10 psychiatric diagnostic categories are presented as a partition of the 2830-patient sample, but the counts total 2840 - ten patients more than the stated N. The accompanying percentages are each individually consistent with a denominator of 2830 (80.32 = 2273/2830, 11.45 = 324/2830, and so on), so the percentage column and the count column were computed against the same N; the excess sits in the counts themselves. The likeliest innocent explanation is that ten patients carry two SSD diagnoses and are counted in two rows, but the paper's inclusion criteria state a single ICD-10 F20-F29 category per patient, so this warrants clarification. Rests only on figures the paper prints

findings.title: Text percentages trailing zero padding
findings.description: At their printed two-decimal precision neither value is expressible as an integer count over 2830: 1893/2830 rounds to 66.89 and 470/2830 rounds to 16.61. Both become consistent at one decimal, so the parsimonious reading is that the authors computed to one decimal and padded a trailing zero to match the two-decimal style used elsewhere. I have recorded this as SUSPICIOUS rather than the tool's IMPOSSIBLE verdict because the discrepancy is one unit in the last printed digit and is fully explained by that padding; it is a presentation defect, not an unreproducible number. Both counts (1893, 470) and the denominator (2830) are stated by the paper, so the check rests on no assumed bound.

findings.title: Statcheck no nhst in prose (Full body text (Results and Discussion))
findings.description: statcheck ran successfully and found nothing to verify. This is a property of the paper's reporting style, not a tool failure: the χ2 values in Table 2 are printed without degrees of freedom and with asterisk markers instead of p-values, and the regression results are given as bare odds ratios without any test statistic. None of this matches the APA grammar statcheck parses. The consequence is that statcheck provides no independent corroboration here - the χ2 verification in this review came instead from recomputing each statistic from its own contingency table, which is a stronger check.
